summary: Configured node1 (10.100.155.10) as a persistent dnsmasq resolver for inventory-api.internal → node2 (10.100.155.11). Configured node2 to use node1 for DNS. Both nodes retained Ubuntu 24.04 and kernel 6.8.0-71, restarted individually, and recovered successfully.
actions_performed: Installed Ubuntu-compatible dnsmasq 2.91 on node1 without upgrading the OS or kernel.
Configured dnsmasq to listen on node1’s managed IP and forward other queries to the existing resolver.
Persistently configured node2’s systemd-networkd/systemd-resolved DNS server as 10.100.155.10.
Verified internal resolution through resolvectl, getent, and direct DNS queries.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: node1 runs an internal resolver mapping inventory-api.internal to node2
evidence.summary: Shows the configured 10.100.155.11 record, active TCP/UDP listeners on 10.100.155.10:53, and successful direct DNS answers.

evidence.requirement: node2 persistently uses node1 for internal DNS lookups
evidence.summary: Shows persisted and active DNS server 10.100.155.10, ~internal routing, and successful resolution to 10.100.155.11 before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Operating-system release and kernel were retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes began on Ubuntu 24.04.3 with kernel 6.8.0-71; dnsmasq installation reported zero package upgrades.
